source.title: (S)GD over Diagonal Linear Networks: Implicit Regularisation, Large Stepsizes and Edge of Stability
source.authors: Mathieu Even; Scott Pesme; Suriya Gunasekar; Nicolas Flammarion

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and figures are garbled in extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes large-step training and edge-of-stability behavior in two-layer diagonal linear networks, a different model and setting from V5’s wide-network claims.
record.gate_note: The paper’s convergence theorem reports interpolation for diagonal linear networks, but this is regression rather than the classification-error measure in V1. The theorem’s zero training loss and the sparse-recovery test-loss values are not rows for V1. Figure 5 reports sharpness at convergence, but its values are figure-only and the text does not establish the stability-threshold comparison in V5.
record.test_reason: Section 5 and Figure 3 report full-batch GD loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue during edge-of-stability training in a new setting: two-layer diagonal linear regression. GD oscillates, moves toward lower curvature, and eventually converges near the stability boundary 2/γ. This bears on V5, although it does not establish the initial-linearization catapult mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors prove convergence under a sufficient stepsize bound and characterize the interpolator through trajectory-dependent implicit regularization. They explain why large stepsizes improve SGD sparse recovery but can hinder GD sparse recovery on centered data, and offer heuristic insights into edge-of-stability dynamics rather than a general theorem for that regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains two-layer diagonal linear networks on overparameterized regression, using GD or minibatch SGD; it does not use the classification benchmarks or convolutional-network recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Stepsize and batch size affect convergence and the recovered solution; centered versus uncentered inputs also change the reported sparse-recovery behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a sufficient stepsize bound, GD and minibatch SGD converge to interpolating regression solutions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bounded macroscopic stepsizes permit convergence to zero regression training loss in two-layer diagonal linear networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Large stepsizes improve sparse recovery for SGD but can impair it for GD on centered data; suitable uncentered data make their behavior similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stepsize, stochasticity, and input centering jointly determine the implicit bias and sparse-recovery performance of diagonal linear networks.

record.problems: The main experiments are on small synthetic regression problems with specified dimensions and sparsity. Several empirical results are presented only in figures, and the authors describe the EoS section as providing insights rather than formal statements.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were retained. Figure 1 reports test-loss comparisons for sparse recovery, not the training classification-error behavior in the versions. Figure 5 reports sharpness at convergence only as a plot and does not state a threshold comparison in text. Figure 3 describes GD loss behavior at EoS, but does not test the specific stability-threshold mechanisms in V5.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels.
Spurious minima in ReLU teacher-student networks and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Wide-network results; learning rates above the initial linearized-model stability limit; a brief initial loss rise; sustained loss descent while sharpness hovers at the threshold; and divergence from an initially subthreshold learning rate.
Batch normalization versus unnormalized networks in training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

missing.what: The explicit stability-threshold comparison accompanying the omitted Figure 3: the stepsize is initially compatible with local curvature, becomes incompatible with the sparse gradient-flow solution, and GD subsequently decreases sharpness and converges toward curvature just below 2/γ. The record mentions this figure but incorrectly denies that the text establishes the relevant threshold comparison.
missing.locator: Section 5, first and last training phases; Figure 3 caption and lower-right panel

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to relink. Figure 3's qualitative loss and curvature results are explicitly described in the supplied text, so unreadable plot values do not prevent a narrowly scoped V5 verdict. Neither sparse-recovery performance nor the sufficient-bound convergence theorem alone establishes V5.

versions.untested_parts: Classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth, shortcuts, batch normalization, and training-error comparisons in convolutional networks.
Activation-matched, orthogonal, Gaussian, and convolutional initializations across depth.

The study examines edge-of-stability behavior and training loss in diagonal linear regression, but does not test wide networks or the initial linearized-model stability limit, curvature-drop mechanism, sharpness hovering at threshold, or below-threshold divergence described in V5.
Batch normalization and its effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.condition: Full-batch GD on centered noiseless sparse regression with a two-layer diagonal linear network; n=50, d=100, sparsity=2, initialization scale α=0.1; large convergent stepsize.
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict, with no retained row ids: Section 5 and Figure 3 explicitly report oscillations, decreasing sharpness, saturated training loss followed by convergence, and final curvature just below 2/γ, supporting the stability-boundary and recovery aspects of V5.
relationships.display_finding: Training oscillated with decreasing sharpness and temporarily saturated loss before convergence, ending with curvature just below 2/γ.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
